lines.text: This chess machine beat Napoleon.
And Napoleon tried to cheat!
Vienna, in the year eighteen-oh-nine.
Everyone's talking about the Turk: a puppet in a turban, sitting on a cabinet full of gears,
that plays chess. And beats everybody!
Before every game, its owner opens the little doors: wheels, levers, gears. Nothing else.
Ladies and gentlemen, no tricks, no cheating!
Napoleon sits down, makes a move... and the Turk answers.
So Napoleon makes an illegal move.
The Turk picks up the piece... and puts it right back.
Napoleon tries it again.
And the Turk, with one swipe, sweeps every piece off the board!
Ha! This machine has more nerve than my generals!
See, the Turk wasn't a machine.
Inside the cabinet was a man: a chess master, hidden among the gears, by the light of a candle.
When they opened the doors, he slid along his seat so no one could see him. And he moved the Turk's arm with a lever.
Ugh... how much longer? It's so hot in here...
Napoleon conquered half of Europe...
but lost a game of chess to a guy stuck inside a piece of furniture.
A very, very tight piece of furniture.
